chapter: Race, critics and the big bands
title: The big bands that passed through Florida, Snookum Russell and Roy Haynes
summary: Sam recalls the many big bands, Carolina Cottonpickers and Louis Russell's band where he met Ray Brown and Roy Haynes.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: A lot of bands, a lot of big bands. There was a
lot of - and it was good too because it was work for all those guys man. See, all those 18-piece bands.

And it was traveling all over the country. There were a lot of bands in and out man. So there was a lot of work, for a lot of musicians man, you know. Jesus Christ, I remember those bands used to come through my home, man.
Oh yeah, you know exactly now the bands they weren't so really big and popular, you know but they was the greatest bands, the Carolina Cottonpickers.

Man those bands, that band was one of the most exciting big bands. They was right up there with the big names man. But they wasn't never...You know and then there was another band called - a band that Ray Brown used to play in, when I first met Ray Brown, Snookum Russell. No, no, not Snookum Russell.
No, it was - yeah it was Snookum, it must be Snookum Russell.
Right because Louis Russell, that's when I met
He was playing in Louie Russell's band. Snookum Russell's band, that's where Ray Brown was playing the bass and where I met him.
So we were teenagers at that time, you see.
There was a whole lot of them bands too.
I mean there was a whole bunch of cats. I mean they could really play, man.

That's right. See, I mentioned that to Roy Haynes during the night he almost fell off the stage. I said 'man do you realize how long I've been knowing you-all my life, you funny looking dude!' I said 'when I saw you, you were in Louis Russell's band'. He almost fell off the stool.
In Florida. Yeah right. Louis Russell's band. So I could go back man.
